draft.title: Gametes and fertilisation
card: Gametes are the sex cells used in sexual reproduction. Males make sperm and females make egg cells.
small cells with a tail, so they can swim to the egg. They carry genetic material from the male parent.
a much larger cell that cannot swim. It holds a store of food that feeds the new organism in its early growth.
Fertilisation is when a sperm joins with an egg. The joined cell carries genetic material from both parents and starts a new organism.
draft.remember: A small swimming sperm joins a large, food-filled egg, and that starts a new organism.

a.q: Why is the egg cell much larger than a sperm cell?
opts: It holds food for the early growth of the new organism
It has a long tail that helps it swim towards the sperm
It carries genetic material from both of the parents
It makes the sperm cell that will join with it
a.why: The egg holds a store of food that feeds the new organism before it can get food in other ways. The egg does not swim, and it carries genetic material from only one parent until fertilisation.
a.clue: Think about what the new organism needs at the very start.

b.q: Under a microscope, Priya sees two cells from a frog. Cell X is small with a tail. Cell Y is large and round with a lot of stored food. Which statement is correct?
opts: X is a sperm and Y is an egg, and fertilisation joins them
X is an egg and Y is a sperm, and fertilisation joins them
X and Y are both eggs, and fertilisation joins them
X is a sperm and Y is an egg, and fertilisation divides them
b.why: A small cell with a tail is a sperm, and a large cell with a food store is an egg. Fertilisation joins the two cells. It does not divide them, and it needs one of each type of gamete.
b.clue: Match the tail and the food store to the right gamete.

a.best: It holds food for the early growth of the new organism

b.best: X is a sperm and Y is an egg, and fertilisation joins them
